summary: The finishing order is an arbitrary permutation, so locating even one requested friend takes linear inspection in the worst case; the accepted stable filter matches that lower bound.

optimality.argument: Consider one friend ID in an arbitrary length-n permutation. Until the algorithm inspects the position containing that ID, any uninspected position could hold it, and an adversary can place it last. A correct worst-case algorithm therefore examines Omega(n) order entries. Set membership and one left-to-right pass perform O(1) expected work per entry, achieving O(n).

replacement_checks.evidence: An adversary may place a requested friend at the final uninspected position of the arbitrary permutation, forcing Omega(n) inspections.
The accepted implementation builds a set of at most eight IDs and performs one expected-constant-time membership lookup per order entry.
Authored cases cover one participant, one friend finishing last, every participant being a friend, boundary IDs, interleaved non-friends, reverse order, and the maximum length 100.
